spots.name: Macroplaza
spots.summary: The Macroplaza or La Gran Plaza is a town square or plaza located in the heart of the city of Monterrey, Mexico. The Macroplaza is the largest Plaza in Mexico and the fifth-largest plaza in the world. It has an extension of 400,000 square metres consisting of various monuments, smaller plazas and gardens.

spots.summary: Fundidora Park is an urban park located in the Mexican city of Monterrey, built in what once were the grounds of the Monterrey Foundry, the first steel and iron foundry in Latin America, and, for many years, the most important one in the region.

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Large, modern museum chronicling the history of Mexico, from pre-Colombian civilizations like the Maya and Aztec, through the colonial period, the revolution, and the modern industrial age.

spots.name: Puente de la Unidad
spots.summary: Puente de la Unidad or Viaducto de la Unidad is a cantilever spar cable-stayed bridge designed by Óscar Bulnes that crosses the Santa Catarina River and connects the cities of Monterrey and San Pedro Garza García in the Mexican state of Nuevo León.

spots.name: Estadio BBVA
spots.summary: Estadio BBVA is an association football stadium located in Guadalupe, a suburb east of Monterrey, Nuevo León, Mexico. Dubbed "El Gigante de Acero", it replaced the Estadio Tecnológico as the home of C.F. Monterrey, ending the club's 63-year tenure at that venue.

spots.name: Antiguo Palacio Federal
spots.summary: Monterrey is unusual among Mexican cities in that it has few stunning, huge, colonial era churches. Most date from the 20th century and have little scenic or historic value. Parroquia Sagrado Corazon is interesting in that it dates from the late 19th century and retains the colonial architecture and style of Mexico's historic churches, but with some of the smooth textures and brighter colors that

spots.name: Palacio del Obispado
spots.summary: The Palacio del Obispado, Spanish for Bishop's Palace, also known as El Obispado or the Bishop's Museum, originally called Palacio de Nuestra Señora de Guadalupe, is an 18th-century colonial building, located in Monterrey, Nuevo León state, Northeastern Mexico.

spots.name: Estadio Universitario
spots.summary: Estadio Universitario, nicknamed El Volcán, is a football stadium located on the campus of the Universidad Autónoma de Nuevo León (UANL) in San Nicolás de los Garza, Nuevo León, Mexico, a municipality in the Monterrey metropolitan area.

spots.name: Estadio Tecnológico
spots.summary: Estadio Tecnológico was a multi-purpose stadium in Mexico, located on the campus of the Monterrey Institute of Technology and Higher Education (ITESM) in Monterrey, Nuevo León. It hosted football and American football games from 1950 to 2017.

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: A regional history museum focusing on the role of the north in Mexico's long and fascinating history. Special exhibits of global interest are also featured.

spots.name: Teatro de la Ciudad
spots.summary: Located on the Macroplaza, the Teatro la Cuidad is a thoroughly modern venue for live theater, classical music, and the performing arts.

spots.name: Muscera
spots.summary: Classic wax museum with figures of political, historic, and popular entertainment personalities. Includes famous Mexican presidents like Benito Juarez as well as pop music stars like Michael Jackson or Juan Gabriel.

spots.name: Museo Acero horno3

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Located inside the enormous blast furnace, the museum has science and technology exhibits with a focus on engineering skills. A full-service restaurant called El Lingote is on the upper level.

spots.name: Parque España
spots.summary: Similar to a YMCA, this is a park focused on fitness and family development. They have a gym, workout facilities, a large pool, an after-school program and classes for aerobics, kickboxing, karate, and more. A pedestrian and bicycle bridge crosses the Rio Santa Catarina, connecting the park to Parque Fundidora. Day passes cost M$200, or monthly plans are available.

spots.name: Cerveceria Fausto
spots.summary: Hip craft brewery with a large outdoor beer garden under the Metro tracks. Beers are much better than most craft breweries in the region because the brewery has lagering facilities and can produce a wider range of beers with cleaner flavor profiles. Some of the best are their dopplebock and a schwartzbier. Dogs are allowed. Occasional live music. Food trucks on site (particularly on weekends).

spots.name: Atope
spots.summary: Upscale Spanish restaurant that's a great date spot because they have live flamenco dancers during dinner and some shareable plates like paella, served in a traditional large shallow pan, or you can choose your own mix of cold and hot tapas (small plates). The house sangria is a good choice, or they have an extensive wine list and a full bar serving large cocktails.

spots.name: Tacos El Compadre

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Basic street taco stand favored by locals for more than 50 years. Recommended by the Michelin Guide. Tortillas are lightly coated in oil and toasted before being stuffed with your choice of fillings including picadillo, ham, guisado con chile rojo, or the specialty of the house (or shack, as the case may be): cabeza de res (steamed cow's head).

spots.name: Mon Paris
spots.summary: Local chain of French coffee shops, another location is near Fashion Drive in Metropolitan Center. Pleasant outdoor dining area, casual atmosphere and a more affordable option compared to the myriad nearby restaurants that cater to the expense account crowd. Crepes for breakfast (or anytime), panini sandwiches at lunch.

spots.name: Sky Bar
spots.summary: Some of the best views of Monterrey from this 58th floor restaurant high atop the Metropolitan Towers. Drinks are creative and good and light finger food is mostly Japanese sushi and sashimi. Indoor seating area with tables available on an outdoor deck. Reservations are required and can be made through Opentable.

spots.name: Ianilli's

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Classic Italian cuisine served in a colonial era building. Classy dining room with rough stone walls, old tile floors and rustic beam ceilings. Oddly enough, they have a life-size sculpture of a horse in the middle of the dining room with a lamp sticking out of its head. Some things are too weird to be made up.

spots.name: Sierra Madre Brewing Company
spots.summary: Modern California-style brewpub with lots of brick, brass, and potted plants. Good, if predictable range of beers including a golden ale, brown ale, IPA and others. Brick oven pizza and burgers. SMBC now has several locations around the Monterrey metro area, but this location was the original.

spots.name: Nomada XXI
spots.summary: Upscale temple to meats, they serve steaks, ribs, barbecue, and burgers. Innovative dishes and you can try a sampler of different meats. Outstanding bar with a wide variety of local artesanal craft beers including their own house brand. Wide selection of artesanal mezcals as well.

spots.name: Koli

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: Regional cuisine of northeast Mexico, modernized and taken up to the level of fine dining. Awarded a Michelin star. Very small intimate dining room, welcomes reservations but charges M$1800 per person for no-shows (so make sure your plans are firm before reserving).

spots.name: La Divina
spots.summary: Traditional Mexican cuisine with an excellent terrace upstairs with view of the Paseo Santa Lucia. If something seems unique or unfamiliar, try it! The idea of noodle tacos seemed strange to me, but they were delicious! (So was the cajeta flan with nuts). Delicious!

spots.name: Unicornio Azul
spots.summary: Monterrey's most popular comedy club. Draws well-known comedians featured on TV (and Netflix) like Franco Escamilla and has a regular lineup of local professional comedians. Occasional Open Mic nights for budding comedians. Light bar fare (wings, fries, tacos).

spots.name: Libros Cafe y Detalles

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Book stores and cafe go together like icing on a cake. Eclectic selection of books, a great upstairs balcony for quiet discrete encounters, and full breakfasts available (not to mention some delicious coffee drinks). Live music outdoors on weekends.

spots.name: Nirvana Rock Joint

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Features 1980s, 90s and some recent music. Good selection of beer, liquor, and appetizers. Free breathalyzer test -- ask the bouncer for a safe taxi if you can't drive. Odd location for a club, in the Plaza Fiesta San Agustin mall, next to Sears.

spots.name: Gallo71
spots.summary: Traditional northern Mexico cuisine, specializing in grilled meats. The ribeye is a whopping 500g (about 18 ounces). The tostadas are grilled the way abuela used to make them. Good selection of artesanal tequilas and local craft beers.

spots.name: Botanero Moritas
spots.summary: Classic cantina established in 1939, extremely clean with great ambience, friendly service, and some of the best traditional northeast Mexican cuisine in town. Tacos are distinctive with darker coloring and rich flavors.

spots.name: Doña Tota

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: You get 2 gorditas, a rather small portion of rice and beans and a drink for M$49 (March 2022). Locations throughout Monterrey, including one inside the central bus station, one in Plaza Mexico and another in Interplaza.

spots.name: La Siberia

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Iconic traditional taqueria with a short simple menu of tostadas and caldo at affordable prices. Fast, sometimes abrupt service with good quality and well-maintained, clean facilities. Great choice for cheap eats.

spots.name: Feelgrow

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Comfortably casual restaurant with a spacious outdoor dining area. The food is a mix of classic Mexican dishes with favorite Italian and American dishes. Open for breakfast (and the chilaquiles are recommended!).

spots.name: Cafe Belmonte Bar

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Cozy rustic coffee shop with great coffee drinks and an eclectic mix of international dishes for breakfast or lunch. Try the German breakfast platter with wurst and spaetzle, or the paninis for lunch.

spots.name: Metapatio

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Large, open-air festival-style party hall with local craft beers, light food, occasional live music, but usually a DJ spinning the tunes. Convenient to hotels near the Macroplaza and Pabellon M.
